title: Evaluation of an unfolded gate
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $g$ be a well-formed gate, let $t$ assign a Boolean circuit on $n$ variables to each gate argument and polarity, let $v$ be a list of Boolean values, and let $x$ be an assignment to the $n$ variables. Suppose that for every argument $a$ of $g$ and each polarity $q$, the circuit $t(a,q)$ evaluates under $x$ to the value of $v$ at index $a$ (using false when that index is out of range) if $q$ is true, and to its negation if $q$ is false. Then unfolding $g$ at polarity $p$ evaluates under $x$ to the value of $g$ on $v$ if $p$ is true, and to its negation if $p$ is false.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is well formed: its argument list has no repetitions and, if it is a NOT gate, has length one
$v$ is a list of Boolean values
$x$ assigns a Boolean value to each of the $n$ variables
For every gate argument and polarity, the assigned circuit evaluates to the corresponding default-false list value or its negation according to the polarity
